headline: Gold Steadies as Fed Rate Path and AI Stocks Frame Volatile Week
author: Wendy Wells

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 26, 2026 at 3:53 PM PST 2 min read
(Bloomberg) -- Gold steadied, as traders weighed the prospect of Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes against a wider market recovery spurred by a rebound in US technology stocks.

Bullion was near $3,565 an ounce, on track for a modest weekly gain after sinking to a 15-month low earlier in a week of choppy trading. Global stocks climbed Thursday as investors in Europe and Asia took their cue from a comeback in artificial intelligence-related equities. US cash markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday.

The yellow metal has remained below $4,000 an ounce since Nov. 11 as traders gauged the Fed's path for combating sticky inflation. It's on track for a third monthly loss of more than 6%, extending a fall from a record high in January that gained pace after the US-Iran war sent energy costs soaring.

The Fed's preferred measure of underlying inflation for October, released Wednesday, reinforced expectations that the central bank will tighten policy when it meets in December. Higher borrowing costs are typically negative for gold, which doesn't pay interest. The market is also weighing the likelihood of further rate hikes early next year if price pressures continue.

Spot gold was little changed at $3,567.67 an ounce at 7:45 a.m. in Singapore. Silver slipped 0.1% to $41.50 an ounce. Platinum rose, while palladium edged lower. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, was on track for a fifth week of gains.
